scope: Proposition 10.2 (No exit and vanishing at true references) of the manuscript “BKT universality for height and planar spin fields” (preprints/BKT-universality-for-height-and-planar-spin-fields-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 216 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5e6a8df09e021c4a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 154. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every sufficiently small prescribed tube radius ρ > 0, the entry choices can be made so that the true-reference plane trajectory stays in this tube at every step and tends to zero. The stopped torus remainders also tend to zero. If a(kc) = 8π, the same entry choices keep all true-reference trajectories (k, a(k)), k ∈ [kc, kc + δ), in that tube for some δ > 0. Each of these trajectories tends to zero; uniform convergence in k is not asserted here.
